Copper-catalyzed SN2’ substitution reactions of chiral propargyl compounds provides an efficient synthetic
method for chiral allenes that have widespread applications in pharmaceuticals and artificial functional materials.
However, compared with the SN2’ reaction catalyzed by palladium, ruthenium, and other noble metals, the
developmentof SN2’reactioncatalyzedbycopperisrelativelydelayedduetoitssensitivitytosterichindrance.Herein
we reported a highly selective copper-catalyzedSN2’ substitution reaction through the use of weakly nucleophilic
zinc reagents. A wide variety of polyfluoroaryl allenes bearing an assortment of functional groups (36 examples)
are compatible with this catalysis system. It is worth noting that chiral polyfluoroaryl allenes can also be efficiently
constructed from chiral propargyl esters via thisSN2’ reaction. A series of mechanism verification experiments and
DFT calculations also provide a basis for the reaction mechanism and the stereo-model of chiral transfer. Moreover,

1.Introduction
Axially chiral allenes are a class of dominant skeletons,
which exist in many natural products, drug molecules,
ligands,andmolecularstructuresofadvancedfunctional
materials.[1–3] Since Burton and Pechmann’s pioneering
work in 1887,[4] the development of synthetic strate-
gies for efficient construction of chiral allenes has
long been a research hotspot in organic synthesis.[5–9]
Among themanydeveloped methods, transitionmetal-
catalyzed SN2’ substitution reactions of chiral propargyl
electrophiles with nucleophiles is favored by synthetic
chemists because of the avoidance of complex chiral
ligands and the ease of preparation of chiral propar-
gyl electrophiles.[10] At present, the SN2’ substitution

reactions catalyzed by palladium, rhodium, and other
noble metals have been relatively mature.[11–18] How-
ever, compared with the former, the copper-catalyzed
SN2’ reaction is relatively delayed, mainly because the
regioselectivity of the reaction decreases as the steric
hindranceofthenucleophileorsubstrateincreases. [19–23]
As a drawback, copper-catalyzed substitution reaction
of propargyl ester has two possible reactive sites (α and
γ positions) that could lead to mixtures of propargyl
orallenylproducts(Figure 1a).[24–26] Therefore,achieving
the synthesis of chiral allenes through highly selective
copper-catalyzedSN2’reactionisstillverysignificantand
challenging.
Polyfluoroarenes widely exist in artificial functional
materials (i.e., pharmaceuticals, materials) due to
their inherent ability to form special intermolecular
interactions.[27–31] In addition, the polyfluoroaryl groups
can also form Z-type interactions with transition
metals when incorporated into ligands, thereby

Precisely because of these important applications,
a number of protocols have been developed for
synthesizing polyfluoroaryl-containing compounds.
However,copper-catalyzedmethodstosynthesizechiral
polyfluoroaryl allenes are still underdeveloped. To our
knowledge, the regioselectivity and stereospecificity
of the reaction have not yet been well controlled
due to the requirement rigid ligand and strong
base.[23] It illustrates the challenge of achieving
chiral polyfluoroaryl allenes with high selectivity
via SN2’ reactions. Herein we report the first regio-
and stereospecific method for the preparation of
chiral polyfluoroaryl allenes from readily available
chiral propargyl esters [34,35] and polyfluoroaryl
zinc reagents [36–39] through copper-catalyzed SN2’
substitution reactions (Figure1c). This catalysis system
successfullysuppressesthecompeting SN2sidereaction
and overcomes the problem of regioselectivity and
stereospecificity.

A series of experiments were conducted to shed
light on the reaction mechanism. First, in order to
further verify whether ligands play a decisive role in
the reaction selectivity, we investigated the effect of
zinc reagents chelated with different ligands. Theγ/α
selectivity of the reaction was decreased with either no
ligand or with the highly steric 1,10-phenanthroline as
the ligand, indicating that the ligand played a decisive
role in the selectivity control (Scheme 4a,e n t r i e s1 –
3). We also found that theγ/α selectivity maintained
when 1, 2-dimethoxyethane replaced diglyme as a lig-
and (Scheme4a, entries 4). These results indicate that
diglyme is most likely coordinated as a didentate ligand
in the γ/α-selective determination step. Subsequently,
we investigated the reaction of equivalent polyfluo-
roaryl copper with propargyl ester1o, and found that
only the polyfluoroaryl copper reagent coordinated
withdiglyme/1,2-dimethoxyethanecangiveagood γ/α
selectivity (Scheme4b). Based on the above outcomes
and literature information, we believe that the excellent
selectivity of the reaction is due to the ability of the
tridentate diglyme to form a relatively stable complex
with copper and zinc reagents, thus weakening their
nucleophilicity and avoiding theSN2 reaction. In order
to further prove the valence state of the copper catalyst
in the reaction, we also conducted a series of EPR
experiments(Scheme 4c).Duringtheprocessofreaction,
we did not observe the Cu(II) signal, which indicates
that there may be no Cu(II) intermediates existed in the
system. We also independently monitored the copper
catalyst and zinc reagent via EPR, and found that the
Cu(II) signal disappeared as the ratio of zinc reagent
to Cu(OTf)2 increased. Based on the above results, we
suspectthattheCu(II)inthereactionmaybereducedto
Cu(I)byzincreagent,alongwiththeformationoffullyflu-
orinatedbiphenyl 6asabyproduct(Scheme 4d,up).[41,42]
Indeed, we did observe the formation of byproduct6in
the reaction system. The control experiments show that
this byproduct can be generated when Cu(OTf)2 reacts
withzincreagent,whichprovesourconjecturethatzinc
reagent reduces Cu(II) to Cu(I). In addition, in order to
further understand the reaction mechanism, the kinetic
studies were also carried out. The results showed first-
order kinetic dependence on Cu(OTf)2 and propargyl
ester 1a, and showed second-order kinetic dependence
on the zinc reagent2a (Scheme 4e). Finally, DFT calcu-
lations were further carried out for theβ-O elimination
step to probe the origin of the chirality transfer. The

On the basis of the above mechanistic studies and

3.Conclusions
In summary, we have developed a regio- and stere-
ospecific copper-catalyzedSN2’substitution reaction for
synthesizing structurally diverse chiral polyfluoroaryl
allenes. The key to success is the use of weakly nucle-
ophilic Zn-ArF reagents with weak nucleophile as the
nucleophileanddiglymewithlowsterichindranceaslig-
and. Moreover, the synthetic utility of this methodology
for the preparation of other valuable polyfluoroarene
containing compounds has also been demonstrated.
Importantly, we proposed a detailed mechanism and
stereo-control model for the reaction based on the
experimental and computational evidences, which pro-
vided a valuable reference for the subsequent study of
